transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining me. As you know, we're looking at a proposed eighth-grade makerspace program for the spring semester that would involve soldering stations, hand tools, and a laser cutter, with 24 students supervised by one STEM teacher, meeting twice weekly. Before I make a final authorization decision, I'd like to hear from each of you on the implementation details relevant to your areas. Could we start with you, STEM teacher? I'd like to understand your perspective on supervising 24 students with this equipment.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to share the results of my room-safety review, which I completed this week. The review found that the makerspace may enroll no more than 16 students, and any session using soldering stations with more than 12 students requires two supervising adults. The draft program form still shows the original numbers of 24 students and one supervising adult, so those will need to be updated to meet the safety requirements.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share the results of my health-record review of the participating students. I found one student with a documented severe nickel allergy. That student may participate only when the program uses nickel-free components, and I must approve the materials list before each session. I should also note that this health-record review has not yet been added to the program file.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to share what I've confirmed with the district technology office regarding the student design files. The district has determined that student design files for this equipment may not use cloud storage. The approved workflow requires an offline design workstation with files transferred by encrypted USB after an IT malware scan. However, I have not yet replaced the cloud-storage instruction in the draft program, so that still needs to be updated.
transcript.speaker: A4

decisions.soldering_supervision: Two supervising adults required for any session using soldering stations with more than 12 students; otherwise one adult suffices
decisions.materials_policy: All components must be nickel-free; Nurse Brooks must approve the materials list before each session
decisions.design_file_method: Offline design workstation with files transferred by encrypted USB after an IT malware scan; no cloud storage

commitments.detail: Update the draft program form to reflect a maximum enrollment of 16 students and the two-adult supervision requirement for soldering sessions with more than 12 students.
Add the health-record review to the program file and ensure the materials list is approved by Nurse Brooks before each session, using only nickel-free components.
Replace the cloud-storage instruction in the draft program with the approved offline workstation and encrypted USB transfer workflow, including the IT malware scan requirement.
Final authorization will be granted once all three updates above are confirmed in the revised program document.
